source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Air Injection Reactor System, p.6T-2

procedures.title: Air Injection Reactor (A.I.R.) system: description
steps: When A.I.R. seems faulty, check engine tune first, especially fuel-air ratio items: crankcase ventilation, carburetor and air cleaner.
notes: Cutting air during the richer decel period prevents backfire; on overrun all the air is dumped through the diverter valve muffler.
At high speed excess air is dumped through the relief valve, located on the pump or on the diverter valve depending on design.
Check valves keep exhaust from flowing back into and damaging the pump, which can happen even in normal running.
Any faulty A.I.R. part or related engine part can raise emissions.

procedures.title: A.I.R. pump drive belt: inspect, adjust and replace
steps: Check the belt for wear, cracks or deterioration and replace if needed.
Check tension with a strand tension gauge and adjust if below 50 lbs.
To adjust: loosen the pump mounting bolt and adjustment bracket bolt, move the pump until the belt is at spec, then tighten the bracket bolt and mounting bolt.
To replace: loosen the same bolts, swing the pump in until the belt comes off, fit the new belt and adjust.

specs.what: A.I.R. belt minimum tension before adjustment

notes: CAUTION: never pry on the pump housing; distorting it causes major pump damage.

procedures.title: A.I.R. drive pulley: replace
steps: Remove the drive belt and replace the drive pulley.
notes: Figure 2 in the manual shows the pump: do not oil the vent hole; the relief valve and pressure setting plug are on the pump.
